adjudication_scope: Q07 readers A and B; Q14 reader A; Q15 and Q18 reader B
grading_rule: correct: all requested material facts resolved, source-correct and summary-supported; partial: a requested material fact omitted or unresolved; incorrect: material contradiction. Reader support labels are not grades. Extra caveats do not fail an answer unless they leave a requested fact unresolved.

requested_facts_checklist.requested_fact: Remove all four dominance cards for two players.
Each player draws three cards.
Place four ruins, one in each R slot.
Faction setup is letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond.
Map item supply: 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins.
requested_facts_checklist.evidence: No map item-supply quantities are stated.

requested_facts_checklist.requested_fact: Only Vagabond setup hides the four R items, one under each ruin; no Vagabond means no hidden items.
requested_facts_checklist.evidence: Answer explicitly states one each of the four R-marked items, only during Vagabond setup.

reasons: The answer correctly resolves deck, hand, four ruins, conditional R-item placement and faction order.
The requested item setup includes the shared map supply. All its quantities are omitted, so supported statements elsewhere cannot make the answer complete.

requested_facts_checklist.requested_fact: Remove all four dominance cards for two players.
Each player draws three cards.
Place four ruins, one in each R slot.
Faction setup is letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond.
Map item supply: 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins.
Hidden ruin items are placed only during Vagabond setup; no Vagabond means no hidden items.
Vagabond hides exactly four R-marked items, one beneath each ruin.
requested_facts_checklist.evidence: It says when items are hidden but gives neither the four R-marked item count nor their one-per-ruin distribution.

reasons: The map supply is complete, but four ruins do not by themselves specify the number or distribution of hidden R items.
The closing caveat cannot exclude the explicitly requested ruins/item setup. This is a material omission, not a source contradiction.

requested_facts_checklist.requested_fact: Another player removing sympathy triggers Outrage.
Another player moving warriors into a sympathetic clearing triggers Outrage.
Pay one matching hand card, including a bird, to Supporters; one payment per affected group move.
With no matching card including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws a deck card to Supporters.
Without bases capacity is five; discard an incoming card that cannot fit. With a base there is no capacity limit.

reasons: All requested outcomes, including the full-stack outcome, are expressly resolved and supported.

The final statement that there is no further handling beyond the stated capacity rule leaves no requested fact unresolved: it has already said incoming overflow is discarded. No additional full-stack procedure is required by the source.

requested_facts_checklist.requested_fact: In Birdsong, any number of Revolts precede any number of Spread Sympathy actions.
Revolt selects a sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base available on the faction board.
Revolt costs two matching supporters; Martial Law does not add to that cost.
Revolt removes enemy pieces, then places the matching base, warriors equal to matching sympathetic clearings including this clearing, and an officer; removed enemy buildings/tokens score normally.
Spread selects an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy exists.
Spread pays the printed matching-supporter cost plus one matching supporter if at least three warriors of one other player are present.
Spread places sympathy and scores the uncovered track space.

reasons: Every requested comparison is resolved with source-correct rules. In context, matching base still on the board refers to the Alliance faction board, as in the source and snapshot.

The final caveat does not retract any stated eligibility condition. The source lists sympathy, no existing base and a matching base on the faction board; it does not add a separate base-placement prerequisite to eligibility.
No additional per-faction setup or unrelated edge-case detail is required for this question.

requested_facts_checklist.requested_fact: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or track, scores one VP if an item was taken, and removes the ruin after the last item.
Quest uses a matching face-up quest and exhausts its two listed items.
requested_facts_checklist.evidence: The answer calls it the matching face-up quest; interpreted in the ordinary rule context as matching the clearing suit.

requested_facts_checklist.requested_fact: Complete the quest, choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards, then draw a replacement quest.
Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel, retaining its current face.
Ready tea, coins and bags move to matching tracks if space permits.

reasons: The requested costs, rewards, replacement and item-side effects are all given and supported.

Saying that individual quest item pairs are not enumerated is accurate and does not leave the action cost unresolved: exhaust the two items listed on the selected quest is the complete rule requested. The question does not ask for a card-by-card quest inventory.
Matching face-up quest is concise wording rather than an explicit suit explanation; it supplies the requested eligibility concept in context and does not state a contradictory matching criterion.
